svg.title: Escape Room Adventure | Seven focused use cases

g.text: Escape Room Adventure | Seven focused use cases
Validate any supplied item against the real inventory.
ActionPlan carries appearingItemIds for existing own-room items.
Game preflights all new transfers before any state/completion change,
then applies state effects and automatically acquires appearing items.
Already-held IDs do not duplicate items or Obtained notices;
legitimate repeatable state effects can still run.
The action's requiredItemId is an exact ID, if present.
Effects never unlock either departure gate; items stay held.
Factory.create constructs the new Game with starting-room entry
and automatic visible-item acquisition before publishing it.
Replace context only on success; the initial message names
the brand-new game's inventory once. No getter acquires items.
Enough items with wrong IDs still fail. Inventory stays unchanged.
An already unlocked door is a no-op before requirement checks.
Output lists all required item names and held required IDs.
Only current Room.exitChallenge is a TriviaLock.
Open fetches once if needed and caches the question.
Submit uses that question; API failure preserves state for retry.
Trivia and ItemLock can complete in either order.
Every open/submit outcome completes a fresh output/render cycle.
Wrong answers retain the active prompt; uninitialized submit
never fetches and has no prompt. API errors also have no prompt.
execute() delegates to Game.move(), with no destination input.
canLeave requires doorLock unlocked AND exitChallenge passed.
Preflight nextRoomId before mutation: present -> successor;
empty -> ESCAPED. Invalid references preserve the current Game.
Present successor: preflight visible-item acquisition, then enter
and acquire atomically. Final completion acquires no extra items.
Output canMove + finalRoom controls one Next room / Escape button.
Capture the full snapshot, then persist through the save port.
Report success only after persistence succeeds.
Schema 4 stores ROOM / INVENTORY item locations,
visibility, action progress, both gates and cached questions.
Its physical shape is unchanged; topology is template-owned.
No nextRoomId or duplicate final-room flag is saved.
Read the save and matching template; restore and validate
Missing/invalid saves preserve the current Game.
Restore cached questions and either ordering of gate progress.
The immutable template version changes with successor structure;
appearance-item configuration must also be version-compatible.
Every predecessor of the restored current Room must have both gates passed.
Current-room gates may still be incomplete in either order.
ESCAPED requires a final current Room and both gates passed.
Restore uses state construction, never enterRoom/acquireItems.
Loading and refresh do not reannounce items already held.
Seven focused input boundaries have seven implementations; every stored collaborator is shown and constructor-injected.
Gameplay/save fetch context.requireCurrent() on each call; no stale Game is cached after loading.
listStories / start / load also work before a game exists. Start/load replace only a validated candidate.
DomainResult(code, changed, resultText) / DomainException -> assembler -> output.present(GameOutputData).
EVERY outcome, including errors and changed=false, completes assembler -> presenter -> EDT model -> View render.
The final EDT completion clears UI busy and the admission guard together, after the result render.
No active game: assembler.fromNoGame(message). GameView receives response data only.
The assembler resolves required-item labels through Game.itemDetails(requiredItemIds), across rooms and inventory.
Story/API/save adapters implement use-case-owned interfaces. All commands run on the serial worker.
Fresh output includes descriptions, available actions, inventory, full door requirements and both gate states.
Movement output is canMove + finalRoom; menu/no-game output sets both false. No topology IDs enter UI output.
Start/load validates one finite path from the starting room covering every room once; reject cycles, invalid references and unreachable rooms.
Game owns automatic ROOM -> INVENTORY transfers; resultText appends only newly obtained item labels.
No independent acquisition command, acquisition ledger or new output field is introduced; schema 4 is unchanged.
